checks.name: the-limit-is-a-side-table-not-a-mode
checks.summary: A4: PASSED. domain.ControlMode's declared constants were enumerated by AST scan over internal/domain and are exactly the seven pre-existing values (allow, pause-intake, pause-claim, graceful-stop, immediate-stop, emergency-stop, cancel) and no more; none of their names or values contains limit, concurren, allocat, throttle or quota. AllocationLimitRepository stores the limit keyed by Control Intent revision, at most once per revision, in the same transaction as SaveControl, exactly as SaveControlRequestedBy does. (a) a request carrying a limit stores the intent and the limit atomically; (b) a replay with the same request_id returns a byte-equal response and writes nothing further (control-row count and limit-row count both unchanged); (c) a replay with the same request_id and a different limit returns application.ErrIdempotencyConflict and leaves the stored limit at its first value -- not by a special case in the limit path but because requestFingerprint covers the whole ControlRequest, exactly as it already does for a changed mode; (d) a request without the field stores no limit row; (e) the row is keyed to the revision the response reported.

checks.name: waiting-reason-projection-is-total
checks.summary: A10: PASSED, with one measured and coordinator-approved shortfall. The projection table is total in BOTH directions over scheduler.AllReasons: every one of the 7 constants maps to exactly one reported bucket, every bucket has exactly one constant behind it, the empty reason an assigned candidate carries maps to no bucket, and five invented reasons (blocked, throttled, over-limit, paused, no-capacity) are refused. All 7 buckets are reported on every read, zero included. waiting.total equals the sum of the buckets and, with 5 considered candidates, waiting.total 4 + planned_assignments 1 = 5. PER-REASON SCENARIOS THROUGH THE SUMMARY: 4 of the 7 are reachable in the running system and each is driven end-to-end -- not-ready (a captured Requirement), already-owned (a ready Requirement that already holds an active Lease), resource-conflict (three ready Requirements linked to one Repository: one assigned, two conflicted, capacity still free), no-runner-capacity (one active Execution with the limit at 1). The other 3 are STRUCTURALLY UNREACHABLE and each names the durable input it lacks: unmet-dependency because domain.Requirement declares no dependency field; not-executable because domain.PriorityAssessment has no persistence port anywhere in the repository; repository-unavailable because the Snapshot models the installation as one synthetic Repository with no failure-count and no isolation-deadline source, and making it reachable is per-Repository availability modelling owned by V2-030's local closure and V2-031's M7 gate. The reachability statement is itself a test: it must cover every constant and claim exactly 4 reachable, so it cannot rot into a list of the convenient ones. No reason value is invented by this task.

checks.name: capture-time-mapping-rule-applied
checks.summary: A14, REWRITTEN FROM MEASUREMENT because the Work Order's premise is false at this commit. A14 asks for the recorded fact that domain.Requirement carries no capture timestamp. MEASURED: it does. V2-073 added CapturedAt with CaptureRecorded() (internal/domain/model.go:193-220), so 'every candidate enters the Snapshot with a uniform zero CreatedAt', 'the aging term is uniform' and 'the effective production ordering is the ID tie-break' are all false here. The implementation follows the measurement, not the record. THE LIMITATION ACTUALLY WORTH RECORDING is the one V2-073 escalated: nothing in production bounds D, the number of seconds by which a flood's capture time precedes a waiter's. V2-030's starvation bound is a true statement exactly for D in [-6500, +3499] seconds, and the one-tick margin StarvationBoundTicks records exists only for D below 1000; the derivation and both endpoint measurements are in internal/scheduler/capture_time_test.go and docs/operations/scheduler-local.md, neither of which this task edited. THE MAPPING RULE V2-073 LEFT TO THIS TASK IS NOW APPLIED: a candidate with no recorded capture time is placed at the Snapshot's Now, age zero. Measured justification: now.Sub(time.Time{}) saturates at 9223372036 seconds -- about 292 years, because time.Duration is int64 nanoseconds -- against a largest priority term of 30000, a factor of 307445, so the zero instant would make every value-less legacy record absolutely preferred. This corrects the dispatch addendum's figure of about 2000 years. The rule's direction is also asserted behaviourally: two ready candidates differing only in capture time, with the value-less one holding the lexically smaller id so it would win any tie, and the single capacity slot goes to the one with the RECORDED older capture time. No substitute timestamp is manufactured: the value is the Requirement's own instant or the Snapshot's Now, never a second clock read and never an event scan.

checks.name: hand-off-the-stale-premise-in-dp-v2-068-d9
checks.summary: Recorded for the next owner, not acted on. dp-v2-068 d9 justifies the single synthetic Repository with the measurement 'There is no Repository aggregate and no enrolled-Runner registry in the store today: RunnerObservationRepository is keyed by id with no list operation, and domain.Requirement carries no repository.' MEASURED: half of that is now false. domain.Repository exists with a status, a source locator and a bounded forge Observation, and RepositoryRepository is a member of application.UnitOfWork (V2-064); a Requirement's Repository is durably recorded in the write-once Requirement-to-Repository link (V2-071), which this task already reads as the contention key. Only the enrolled-Runner half still holds: RunnerObservationRepository is still keyed by id with no list operation, so there is still nothing to enumerate a real pool from. WHAT THAT UNLOCKS AND WHY IT WAS NOT TAKEN: feeding the real link and the real Repository records into Snapshot.Repositories -- one entry per referenced Repository, omitted or isolated when the Repository is retired or its executability is not executable -- would make repository-unavailable observable, taking the reachable reason count from four to five, and would let the report distinguish 'this Repository cannot be worked' from 'this Requirement is not ready'. That is per-Repository availability modelling, which is V2-030's local closure and V2-031's M7 gate, so claiming it here would duplicate or re-open another task's scope. It is measured, recorded and left; the synthetic Repository stays and repository-unavailable stays unreachable until the owner of that half takes it. This is the FOURTH stale premise in wo-v2-068/dp-v2-068: the others are A14's 'domain.Requirement carries no capture timestamp' (false since V2-073), A20's 'ci/components.json declares application's dependencies as [domain] and scheduler's as []' (measured [domain, infra, release] and [domain]), and d13's claim that the internal/quota edge is undeclared (the infra edge is declared). Written into docs/operations/allocation-local.md under 'Hand-off: dp-v2-068 d9's measured premise is stale, and what that unlocks'; make docs is green.
